questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english speaking country, where the culture wasn't too different, but I could still experience something new.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Free pick up from the airport and an orientation session at uni on the first day of the intro week

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Don't exactly remember, but think I could choose a one bedroom apartment, a shared room and a private room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: On big communal kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If living at Queen Mary there is only one communal kitchen for everyone. The kitchen was not very clean and I personally didn't enjoy using it. Additionally you need to bring/buy all you own bedding and kitchenware, which feels a bit wasteful. Also, the check in was really chaotic and disorganized and took a long. Otherwise the room was nice and had all the furniture you need and it's nice and close to campus which is a huge plus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I ended up paying almost 3000kr extra in rent, because of a really bad conversion rate. The guide to transferring money is not that cleat and there wasn't really any help to get from the staff at Queen Mary/USYD. You need to transfer the money in AUD, to get the right conversion fee, which should have been more clearly stated.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You couldn't really now the schedule of each course before you went, so be prepared to change some courses when you get there because you have clashes in you schedule.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Don't exactly remember, but it was through here website. Remember it wasn't that difficult

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A step by step guide and your USYD advisor

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted, but had to change on when I got there because some of my courses where clashing

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have back up courses ready

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Only pick 1-2 courses with lab work. Lab work is mandatory and takes a lot of time. Doing more courses will increase your workload and make you schedule quite packed and unflexible.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The same as UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Higher in-semester workload (quizzes, assignments, reports etc) as the exam doesn't count for 100% of the grade and you have assessment tasks all through the semester

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biochemistry of humane disease
Neuropharmacology 
Concepts in chemistry of biological molecules
Sport and learning in Australian culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sport and learning in Australian culture was a great, easy and fun course. Very few lectures, no exam and easy assessment tasks. However, the best part was that you got to attend a lot of different field trips like seeing a rugby match, AFL, horse racing, hiking etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, clubs about everything you can image and events arranged by the student union USU

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Did a beginners tennis course for women which was great and become a USU member. It gets you acces to a lot of events and sometimes free food on campus

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Sydney, go to the Blue Mountains, Queensland, visit Uluru, Melbourne

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not anything really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The australian people are really open and friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you have a lot of classes it's worth living close to campus, otherwise there are nicer areas to live in

Pick some "fun" courses where you get to experience Australia if you can. Could be the "Sport and learning in Australian culture"

Try and make you schedule as easy as possible by picking courses that might be a year below you or are similar to some you've already had at home. Being on exchange is a lot and you want to do and experience as much of Sydney and Australia as you can

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing school work and being social and wanting to do and experience everything all the time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Remember to also take some downtime and relax

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
